desks.Dividends: Microsoft, ex Thu Nov 19 at $0.98 per quarter (pay Dec 10), is the only declared watchlist ex-date in the window, its 24th consecutive annual increase. Apple's dividend is still undeclared, with declaration watch on the Nov 2 earnings print; Nvidia's next declaration normally accompanies its Nov 17 print, pointing to an early-December ex-date outside the window. SPY and QQQ point to mid-December on pattern only, Tesla pays no dividend, and no cuts or specials were found among watchlist names.
desks.Earnings: Apple reports Mon Nov 2 after close (release 1:30 p.m. PT, call 2:00 p.m. PT) with an options-implied move of about 4.3%. Microsoft beat Oct 28 after close, revenue $92.3 billion (+19%), non-GAAP EPS $4.89 (+18%), Azure +48%, then fell 0.16% Oct 29 and about 1.6% Oct 30 on indicative marks. Nvidia's date is Tue Nov 17 after close on the company's Oct 28 announcement; a Nov 18 secondary estimate conflicts with it, and the Nasdaq calendar gave no confirmation this run, so it is not cited as the confirmer. Tesla reported Oct 21.
desks.Futures: EIA data split the energy complex: crude inventories fell 1.9 million barrels to 410.6 million for the week ended Oct 23, against a poll expectation of a small build, and distillates fell 1.5 million barrels, while gasoline stocks rose 3.9 million barrels and natural gas storage built 80 Bcf, above the roughly 70 Bcf survey estimate, pushing gas below $3.00. Ukraine resumed strikes on Russian refining Oct 30, and Russian freight rates remain at record highs. Next catalysts: OPEC+ Sun Nov 1, EIA petroleum Wed Nov 4, EIA gas Thu Nov 5. Grains are still digesting the bearish October WASDE supply build, with December corn at a four-month low close despite a marketing-year-high wheat export sale.
desks.Parity: No published put-call or box parity violation was found for the watchlist this week. The methodology item to watch is the S&P Dow Jones Indices growth/value revamp, effective at the annual reconstitution before the open Dec 21, 2026, with pro-forma files Dec 4: value scoring adds intangibles-adjusted book value and free-cash-flow-to-price, and 12-month price momentum drops from growth ranking. The cited $375 billion or more in passive funds tied to affected style benchmarks is an analyst estimate, not an S&P figure, and the change reclassifies style-index membership, not S&P 500 headline membership. The Nasdaq-100 Fast Entry proposal dates to Feb 2026, with no final rule found.
desks.Premium: Apple's Nov 4 expiry at 43.1% implied volatility against 13.5% realized is event pricing ahead of the Nov 2 print, not a mispricing signal. Index and single-name front implied volatility outside Apple sits at or below trailing realized volatility: SPY 13.6% versus 10.3% realized, QQQ 18.0% versus 20.1%, Microsoft 19.3% versus 20.1%, Nvidia 27.5% versus 31.0%, Tesla 30.1% versus 40.0%. Nov 4 expiries run higher across names, consistent with midterm-election event premium, and an apparent SPY put-call parity gap in post-close marks is a non-synchronous data artifact, not a tradeable violation. Implied-volatility rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names.
desks.Quant lab: Six new candidates were appended to the ledger as rows 182-187: two WATCH adds, an honest-negative transformer-sentiment volatility paper and a tail-forecast evaluation correction noting that exceedance count, not observation count, is the effective sample size, plus four ARCHIVEs on band discipline. No TEST and no INTEGRATE movement this run; the only TEST candidate remains number 171, a packaged conditional-volatility model set, and the sentiment negative makes three honest negatives in the volatility-forecasting lane, where simple models plus VIX keep beating complex ones.

headline: Daily research brief — Friday, October 30

items.detail: Two tankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz on consecutive days, MT Arzanah on Oct 29 and MT Louise 1 on Oct 30, and Brent rose $2.76 to $117.61 with WTI up $2.16 to $104.16 on Oct 30. No Hormuz closure is confirmed, and claims of strikes on Saudi facilities, including Ras Tanura and Abqaiq, are UNVERIFIED in the sourced reporting, so the move reads as a geopolitical risk premium rather than a confirmed physical supply cut. The curve is steeply backwardated, with a December-January Brent spread near $3.88 and a Brent-WTI nearby premium near $12-13, and OPEC+ meets Sun Nov 1 with December targets expected unchanged; a quiet weekend supports premium fade, while a confirmed closure or facility damage would upgrade this to a physical-supply event.
items.title: Hormuz attacks repriced oil on risk premium, not confirmed supply loss

items.detail: Apple reports Mon Nov 2 after close, with consensus EPS of $1.98 and revenue of $112.95 billion, and the Nov 4 expiry straddle implies a move of about 4.3%. Front implied volatility of 43.1% is about 3.2 times trailing realized volatility of 13.5%, and fiscal fourth-quarter reports have risen only 6 of 17 times with a median move of -0.9%. The swing factor is the December-quarter guide and the memory-cost and margin read, not the September quarter, which Apple already guided at 9-11% revenue growth. That combination argues against paying premium into the print.
items.title: Apple Nov 2 is the window's only live earnings binary

items.detail: Indicative post-close marks put QQQ down 3.5%, Nvidia down 4.2% and SPY down 2.1% on Oct 30, on top of the Oct 29 after-hours damage from Amazon and Intel and today's oil spike; these levels are indicative, not settled closes, because underlying quotes drifted between post-close pulls. Outside Apple, front implied volatility sits at or below trailing realized volatility for QQQ, Microsoft, Nvidia and Tesla, so there is no volatility edge in either direction. Two cautions: a single large day next week would leave the QQQ and Nvidia realized baselines unreliable, since one day already drives 28.8% and 28.5% of their 20-day windows, and Nov 3-4 expiries carry event premium consistent with the Nov 3 midterm election, though that attribution is not confirmed.
items.title: A hard growth selloff, but volatility outside Apple looks fairly priced

items.detail: FRED prints dated Oct 29 put the effective fed funds rate at 3.88%, inside the 3.75-4.00% target range held at the Oct 28 FOMC decision, the 2-year at 4.61% and the 10-year at 4.98%, a 2s10s spread of +37 basis points after modest flattening from +41 at the start of the 60-day window. SOFR at 3.94% sits 6 basis points over the effective fed funds rate, a normal overnight funding print with no stress signal. The 10-year is off its 5.31% window high, but near 5% it remains a valuation headwind for long-duration names such as Nvidia and Tesla on discount-rate grounds, and there is no inversion signal to offset that read.
items.title: Rates: 10-year at 4.98%, curve sloping up, funding calm
